newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down on Swiss sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on Swiss sales.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended Wednesday slightly down from its previous New York close following light selling from Swiss players in afternoon trade, bullion dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$348.90/349.40 an ounce on Wednesday against New York's US$349.20/70 close on Tuesday.
"There was light Japanese buying in the morning," said one bullion dealer.
Swiss selling in the latter half of the day pushed gold prices down, but dealers said there were no identifiable trends. Trading activity was said lackadaisical throughout the day.
Gold dealers said gold would continue to trade within a narrow range of $348-$350 per ounce, unless U.S. funds triggered price movements overnight.
"We really just have to see what the funds do," said one senior bullion trader.
Physical demand remained subdued by seasonal lack of interest despite the drop in prices, but could pick up if gold sank further to $345 per ounce or so, traders said.
Local gold ended HK$11 higher at HK$3,232 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained dropped to -4.50 from its previous fix at -4.00.
